_comment: Validation limits for untrusted input. Authority: ADR-0003 §11 (envelope caps, depth limits), ADR-0014 N-10 (pre-authentication caps), ADR-0002 §11.6 (backpressure), ADR-0007 (identifier sizes). Every field here is enforced BEFORE any allocation proportional to a declared length. A violation is a typed reject with a PROTO.* code, never a truncation, never a pad, and never a silent accept.

envelope._c4_note: 1200 B is the worst-case IPv6 path MTU minus headers, NOT the IPv4 576 B floor: C4 is never fragmented and IPv6 forbids in-network fragmentation.
envelope._c2_inline_note: Lower than the envelope cap on purpose, so a single policy bundle cannot monopolise a stream. Larger documents are announced by reference and pulled.

capability._max_name_bytes_note: 32, not 24. CF-6 amended ADR-0014 N-11 from 24 to 32 on 2026-08-27 and deliberately did NOT rename the offending token, because it is security_relevant and a rename is an S-37 compatibility event. capabilities.json says 32, capabilities.cddl says [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,31}, and the capability registry itself contains dns_config_dies_with_tunnel at 27 bytes -- so a validator honouring 24 rejected a Phase-1-MANDATED token. Recorded as an open contract defect in ownership.md §4.3 with a live workaround in production code; closed here in registry_version 2.
